## Rationale

The claim that Japanese interest rates will rise to 2.5% by 2026 is inconsistent with Japan's structural economic constraints, including demographic challenges (aging population, low fertility), historical monetary policy trends (ultra-low rates for decades), and deflationary pressures. The Bank of Japan has demonstrated cautious, gradual tightening rather than abrupt normalization, and no major economic catalysts (e.g., sustained inflation, fiscal consolidation) are present to justify such a sharp increase. Specialist analyses across demography, energy, capital markets, and trade all converge on this conclusion, citing the BoJ's policy aversion and global financial dynamics as key barriers.
